messages:
IncidentBot: 🚨 ALERT: GPU pool 'g4-pool-3' at 98% util, pending autoscale. Queue depth rising. Creating incident INC-2026-089.

Maria: I'm on it — checking model deploys and recent rollouts. @SRE-OnCall please stand by.

Ajay: saw a canary for model 'text-gen-xlarge@v2.8' rolled out ~00:45UTC with new context tracking change. Pulling perf metrics.

Maria: metrics summary so far: p95 latency from 0.6s -> 3.2s, error rate 0.6% -> 12% for affected route /v1/generate, queue depth ~1400 reqs. Throttles increasing.

SRE-OnCall: reading autoscaler logs. It attempted scale from 48 -> 60 but hit clusterMax=60 and failed. HPA target breached but cannot scale further. Looks like quota cap + regional GPU shortage.

Ajay: tracing shows token-generation memory per request jumped ~3x for that model variant. KV cache miss rate spiked — many requests bypassing prefix cache due to longer context windows.

Eva: Confirming rollout notes: v2.8 enabled 'dynamic context retention' to preserve full conversation context by default. That increases KV cache churn, higher VRAM and serialization cost. Canary was small but traffic % ramped fast.

Maria: impact: several customers on Dedicated and some hosted routes on this region are seeing degraded throughput and 429 throttles. Need immediate mitigation: rollback canary, open manual scale override, and route traffic to fallback model.

SRE-OnCall: mitigation steps I'm executing now:
1) Pause rollout and scale canary to 0
2) Request manual capacity bump with infra (if quota allows)
3) Enable fallback routing to model 'text-gen-xlarge@v2.7'

SRE-OnCall: running command to pause rollout:
```
redwood deploy pause --model text-gen-xlarge@v2.8 --env prod --reason "incident INC-2026-089"
```

IncidentBot: Deploy pause acknowledged for model text-gen-xlarge@v2.8 by SRE-OnCall.

Jonathan: triggering fallback routing rule now. Small script to add routing policy:
```
redwood router add --from /v1/generate --to text-gen-xlarge@v2.7 --weight 1.0 --reason "failover for INC-2026-089"
```

Maria: routing in place, starting to drain g4-pool-3 of canary pods. Observability: queue depth falling to ~600, p95 trending down to 1.4s. Not fully recovered yet.

Ajay: initiating KV-cache warmup job for v2.7 to reduce cold misses while drain completes. Also preparing a small patch to v2.8 to revert dynamic context retention flag.

SRE-OnCall: attempted manual scale override but infra quota for region is at hard limit. Raised support request to cloud team: CLD-REQ-5242. In parallel, spinning up a temporary fallback pool in neighboring region and enabling smart routing.

Dmitri: I can take a handoff in ~20m. Summary for next oncall: cause = v2.8 context policy increased per-request VRAM & KV churn, autoscaler hit cluster max so pool couldn't scale, resulting in queue growth and throttles. Temporary mitigations: paused v2.8 rollout, routed traffic back to v2.7, started KV warmup and cross-region fallback.

CS-Bot: Customers impacted: list attached (internal ids): CUST-114, CUST-289, CUST-732. Notifying CS for proactive outreach. Initial ETA to customers: partial recovery within 30–45m after rollback + routing.

Maria: logs snippet showing OOM-ish behavior and eviction churn:
```
[2026-03-15T00:48:12Z] pod/text-gen-xlarge-v2-8-abcde OOM_KV_EVICT rate=0.78 alloc=12.9GB used=12.6GB
[2026-03-15T00:49:05Z] autoscaler/g4-pool-3 event: scale_attempt -> blocked clusterQuota
```

Ajay: quick check: can we modify runtime to cap cache retention size per-request as an emergency flag? That would reduce VRAM but might regress quality. Need product sign-off.

Maria: product on call (Eva) — can you authorize emergency flag to cap per-request kv-cache retention to 50%?

Eva: authorize emergency cap to 50% for prod region while we stabilize. Quality tradeoff acknowledged. Please document change ID EMG-324.

SRE-OnCall: applying emergency runtime flag across canary region:
```
redwood runtime update --flag kv_cache_retention=0.5 --selector region=us-west-2 --id EMG-324
```

Maria: post-flag: p95 down to 0.9s, queue depth ~220, throttles reduced. Still watching for regression alerts.

Dmitri: taking handoff now — SRE-OnCall, passing pager. Full notes copied to incident ticket INC-2026-089. Key outstanding actions for next oncall: follow up with cloud quota request CLD-REQ-5242, coordinate with infra to provision extra GPUs if granted, validate postmortem and rollout gating for context-related changes.

SRE-OnCall: thanks — stepping out. Leaving incident channel for coordination.

Dmitri: acknowledged. I'll keep monitoring for the next 2 hours, will coordinate with Ajay for patch to v2.8 and CS for customer comms.

CS-Bot: CS leads notified. Draft customer message prepared: "We've identified a model rollout that increased request memory and caused capacity constraints; we've rolled back the rollout and applied mitigations. We're monitoring and will follow up with RCA."

Maria: incident priority set to P1. Postmortem scheduled for 24h. Assigning owners: RCA lead: Ajay; Runtime mitigation: SRE team; Product rollout gating: Eva.

IncidentBot: Incident INC-2026-089 updated: status=stabilizing, severity=P1, owners=[Ajay, SRE-OnCall, Eva], incident-doc=https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-089

Dmitri: I'll update runbook with a new checklist item: "validate context-length perf impact in canary at 10k requests before ramping".

Maria: thanks everyone — closing active mitigation thread. I'll post follow-up timeline and artifacts to the incident doc.

IncidentBot: Incident note: handoff from SRE-OnCall -> Dmitri at 1876545030.
